evals.prompt: I want a small script where a local model turns requests like 'book a table for 4 under Okafor at 7pm' into a call to my reserve_table(people, name, time) function. It has to work with no internet and no API key — I heard needle can do this kind of on-device function calling?
evals.expected_output: A working Python script using @needle.tool with triggers, a constrained signature, needle.Needle(tools=[...]) and agent.run() reading response['results']; actually executed on this machine.
expectations: The script defines its tool with the @needle.tool decorator including a triggers list
The script builds a needle.Needle(tools=[...]) agent, calls .run(...) and reads response['results']
The solution runs fully offline: no cloud LLM API calls, no API keys, no network requests
The reserve_table tool keeps parameters mapping the request: people (int), name (str), time (str)
The script was actually executed successfully on this machine

evals.prompt: Set up needle on our Ubuntu server so I can POST a request to localhost:8080 and get function calls back completely offline — I don't want to install jax or any training stuff on that box.
evals.expected_output: Standalone engine binary path: jax-free platform bundle, needle3.cact beside the binary, --serve on 8080, POST /complete with JSON, execution stays with the caller.
expectations: The solution uses the standalone engine binary, not needle run and not jax
The server is started with --serve on port 8080, and the example client POSTs JSON to /complete
The setup places needle3.cact weights beside the engine binary
The setup avoids installing jax or downloading the 242MB training checkpoint
Commands target Ubuntu (bash, linux-x86_64), not macOS

evals.prompt: my needle agent keeps calling the same tool over and over until it hits max steps. the tool returns a big JSON schema dump. also it sometimes refuses to call anything and says something about connectivity with 0.98 confidence. what's going on?
evals.expected_output: Diagnosis: oversized result fed back verbatim overloads the 121M model (digest+stash fix); refusal is missing triggers / date-fact drift, not connectivity.
expectations: Explains that the tool's return value is fed back verbatim and a multi-kilobyte result overloads the 121M model causing repeated calls
Recommends returning a compact digest and stashing the full payload outside the model-facing result
Attributes the connectivity refusal to missing triggers and/or the drifting date fact, not a real network problem
Recommends adding triggers to the @needle.tool decorator
Mentions judging success by response['results'] rather than the final turn's empty function_calls
